items.title: Josiah Gluck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 13, 2022
items.q: Sinatra’s music, you’re talking about those great recordings done at Capitol Studios with their live chambers

ctx.x: Well that Syn drum was louder than anything. Louder than the vocal, and as an engineer I’m wondering does that pop out for you as something — or what am I trying to say — if you had been the engineer on that date would you have thought why — you want the thing that loud?

I wouldn’t have minded it and I think everything I’ve been doing over the years, any engineer, everything is a stylistic and aural learning curve. That is, that to me is — sonically it’s a hook the way the chorus is a hook. One thing — I don’t know why this one just pops in my head, there was a hit a number of years ago with Aaron Neville and Linda Ronstadt, “Don’t Know Much.” I am certainly not going to sing it, but their tight harmony to me is the hook, it’s the signature of that song. So on the Fine Young…

You’ve been a producer as well and I’m wondering if there’s been occasions where you’ve been an engineer with another producer and because of your experience you think this is not the way to go that this producer is suggesting. And do you ever butt heads?
